items.title: Prediction: This Unstoppable Stock Will Rejoin the $2 Trillion Club by 2027
items.summary: Broadcom has become a leading supplier of data center chips and components to the artificial intelligence industry.

items.title: 3 Growth Stocks to Add to Your Roster
items.summary: Growth boosts valuation multiples, but it doesn’t always last forever. Companies that cannot maintain it are often penalized with large declines in market value, a lesson ingrained in investors who lost money in tech stocks during 2022.

items.title: Qualcomm Stock Looks Cheap, But Is The Discount Deserved?
items.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) trades at about $176 a share, down about 14% over the past three months and up 12.4% over the past twelve. At 20.1 times earnings against an S&P 500 median of 22.9, a profitable chip designer sits below the market. The question is whether that is a good business on sale or a fair price for a business under real pressure.

items.title: Marvell Technology vs. Broadcom: Comparing Revenue Trends Between These Artificial Intelligence Companies
items.summary: Broadcom's latest quarter revenue hit $29.6 billion — nearly 11 times Marvell's $2.7 billion — with both companies posting steady gains over the past two years.

items.title: The Portfolio You Need to Generate $500 a Month in Dividend Income
items.summary: Generating $500 a month from dividends sounds straightforward until you see how wildly the required capital swings depending on which stocks you pick and which trade-offs you are willing to accept.

items.title: Can Marvell Stock Make You Money Before Its Hyperscaler Deal Pays Off?
items.summary: Marvell Technology (MRVL) trades at $235.01, and it has expanded its agreement with a key hyperscaler, a deal analysts size at up to $120 billion of revenue over about six and a half years. Most of that money, though, arrives after the fiscal 2028 outlook you would be paying for today.

items.title: The Case for Broadcom Over Nvidia Strengthens in September
items.summary: Both Broadcom and NVIDIA just posted blowout AI quarters, yet rising Treasury yields and compressing multiples are forcing investors to pick sides. The answer may surprise anyone still treating these two as interchangeable AI bets.

items.title: OpenAI Picked Broadcom for Its First Custom AI Chip. The Race for Number Two Just Got Dangerous.
items.summary: OpenAI just disclosed a Samsung chip partnership, and investors are already punishing Broadcom stock for it. But the key question nobody is asking is whether Samsung actually took anything Broadcom had.
